Issue 1

🚀 Houthis Fire Missile at Riyadh Financial District…PIF Tower Hit, Oil Prices Rise

Key summary
  • Yemen's Houthi rebels launched a missile attack on November 19 (local time) targeting Riyadh's financial district (King Abdullah Financial District), the Saudi capital, damaging the skyscraper housing the Saudi sovereign wealth fund (PIF) headquarters.
  • The Saudi-led coalition separately announced it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen's Houthis heading toward southern Saudi Arabia, with additional 'potential danger' alerts issued for the Abha and Khamis Mushait areas.
  • The Qatari and Kuwaiti foreign ministries and the GCC Secretary-General issued statements strongly condemning the attack on the Riyadh financial district, confirming moves toward Gulf regional security coordination.
  • Assessments emerged that the Iran-US war is leaving a 'lasting mark' on global energy markets.

Issue 2

⚔️ US-Iran War Costs Surge, Risk of Escalation Persists

Key summary
  • A US Department of Defense budget official reported to the Senate Armed Services Committee that the cost of the US-Iran war has reached about $48.3 billion (approximately 64-65 trillion KRW); this includes ammunition, equipment replacement, and operational costs, but excludes repair costs for US military bases in the Middle East damaged by Iranian attacks, suggesting future costs will rise further. The US Senate, led by Republicans, rejected a resolution to limit President Trump's war powers regarding Iran.
  • A US government watchdog pointed out that the prolonged Iran war has worsened shortages in US military ammunition stockpiles.
  • Reports emerged that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is trying to persuade President Trump to resume military operations against Iran.

Issue 3

💥 Israel Launches Ground Operation in Central Gaza, Crossing the 'Yellow Line'

Key summary
  • The Israeli military announced it launched its first large-scale ground offensive crossing the control line known as the 'Yellow Line' in central Gaza, expanding occupied territory. The operation resulted in additional Palestinian deaths and injuries.
  • Iran's Foreign Ministry issued a statement strongly condemning Israel's 'crimes' against Palestinians in Gaza.
  • Iran requested an emergency meeting of Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) foreign ministers with the lifting of the Gaza blockade on the agenda, while Save the Children warned that children in Gaza face 'unprecedented danger'.

Issue 4

🤝 Qatar's Amir Makes Official Visit to Germany…Strengthening Strategic Investment and Energy Cooperation

Key summary
  • Qatar's Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani began an official visit to Germany; the chairmen of the Qatar Chamber and the Qatar Business Association (QBA) assessed that the visit would provide new momentum for Qatar-Germany bilateral strategic relations and investment cooperation.
  • It was emphasized that the Qatar-Germany energy partnership helps position Qatar as a 'reliable global energy source,' highlighting Qatari LNG's role in ensuring stable supply to Europe.
  • Sheikha Al Mayassa described the Qatar-Germany cultural partnership as an example of 'human diplomacy,' and Qatar's Government Communications Office (GCO) and the Qatari Embassy in Berlin held a promotional event for the 2027 Web Summit Qatar.

Issue 6

🛢️ Tensions Persist in the Strait of Hormuz…Tanker Incident and Oil Price Fluctuations

Key summary
  • Iran's Navy announced that a tanker (supertanker) that violated maritime regulations caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, continuing concerns over vessel safety in Hormuz.
  • Amid continued reports of tanker attacks, international oil prices (Brent crude) rose slightly (0.69%, per barrel), while US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said that energy supply through Hormuz remains 'inconspicuously' maintained but noted that 'the situation has changed.'
  • Analysis emerged that Yemen and the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait are rising as a 'second maritime front' in the US-Iran confrontation, with reports that Iran's attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain are intensifying the escalation surrounding Hormuz.

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
